{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABe_aiSg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhIgGHk", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 375, "title": "Improve contenteditable voice dictation compatibility and prevent insertion errors from stopping recording", "body": "## Goal

Improve **browser-page voice dictation into rich text editors / `contenteditable`**, so users can dictate into editors like the X (Twitter) post composer, ChatGPT web composer and Claude composer reliably.

**Start with editor-type-aware, site-agnostic handling.** Do not build a pile of site-specific X/ChatGPT/Claude adapters up front. Add narrow site-specific fixes later, based on reproduced failures.

Two core outcomes:
1. Inserting confirmed transcribed text works with ordinary and framework-managed editable fields, preserving their internal editor state, caret, user text, and undo history where supported.
2. A transient insertion/DOM-reconciliation failure does **not automatically abort otherwise healthy microphone capture or ASR**. Recognized text is retained for safe recovery, without duplicate or wrong-target insertion.

## Verified current behavior / relevant code

- [`extension/web-voice-content.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/web-voice-content.js)
  - `editable()` explicitly **rejects** `[data-lexical-editor]`, `.ProseMirror`, `.ql-editor` and editors with complicated descendant elements.
  - The field microphone's output handler uses synthetic `beforeinput`, then **direct Range/text-node mutation**, then synthetic `input`.
  - It remembers `owner.expected` from `textContent` and `owner.range`; a framework re-render, changed markup, or changing selection can raise an error, then `abort(error.message)` ends the whole dictation session.
  - `selectionchange`/`input` handling and DOM target checks already exist; preserve their safety intent while making them resilient.
- [`extension/page-agent.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/page-agent.js) implements a **separate** text insertion path for `FocusedInputTextOutputNode`, with similar rich-editor exclusions and direct DOM editing. Reuse the same insertion behavior / primitives in both routes where practical, **without merging their security authorization models**.
- [`extension/web-voice-capture.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/web-voice-capture.js) independently stops capture on real audio/mic failures (permission revoked, audio track ended, relay backpressure/watchdog, etc.). **Keep these genuine stop conditions** separate from text insertion problems.
- [`extension/web-voice-background.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/web-voice-background.js) and `web-voice-runtime.js` own document-scoped sessions, capabilities and output-relay lifecycle. Maintain security, bounded queues and ownership.

## Desired implementation

### A. Extend editable detection and targeting

1. Allow **legitimate writable** `contenteditable` inputs used by rich editors, including ProseMirror, Lexical, Draft.js and Quill-like DOMs, rather than blanket-blocking them.
2. Detect the **actual active editable root** (which may be nested, dynamically replaced or have a shadow/editor wrapper); do not treat arbitrary surrounding `contenteditable` descendants or unrelated widgets as independent targets.
3. Preserve strict safety restrictions: no password/authentication/payment/OTP/sensitive forms, hidden/inert/readonly/disabled editors, unrelated inputs, unauthorized frames or non-focused pages; never send dictation to another element as a guess.
4. Detect user-intended target changes and re-renders safely. Preserve the correct caret/selection when possible; if a target is removed or replaced and identity is ambiguous, **pause delivery and require user re-selection**, rather than silently inserting into the wrong editor.

### B. Insert text through editor-compatible editing paths

5. Extract/reuse a small **text insertion strategy** usable by both the injected website microphone and `FocusedInputTextOutputNode`. Keep ordinary `input`/`textarea` behavior working, and support general `contenteditable` as a distinct strategy.
6. For rich editors, prefer a browser editing operation that lets the editor update its **own document model and Undo history** (e.g. feature-detected `document.execCommand('insertText', false, text)` where actually effective); account for its deprecated, inconsistent behavior. **Do not assume a successful boolean return or a synthetic `beforeinput`/`input` event means the application state was updated.** No blind DOM mutation fallback for framework-managed editors that will overwrite/revert it.
7. Preserve the current caret or selected range (replace selection when appropriate), existing text, multiline text/newlines where supported, repeated utterances and incremental committed segments. Never type into the wrong editor, overwrite unrelated user content, or accidentally submit the form.
8. Only insert **committed/final transcription** into rich editors by default. Do not repeatedly replace a framework editor with volatile interim ASR previews.
9. Check that the insertion is reflected in the actual editor state/observable content as reliably as feasible; handle asynchronous re-render/reconciliation. If insertion cannot be confirmed, report an **ambiguous outcome** rather than blindly retrying it and risking duplication. Do not fabricate trusted keyboard events or bypass site security checks.

### C. Decouple insertion failure from recording / provide safe recovery

10. Distinguish **capture/ASR fatal failures** from **destination/insertion failures**. A temporary editor re-render, missing caret, canceled `beforeinput`, rejected insertion or lost editor focus should **not by itself cancel valid microphone capture and inference**.
11. Maintain a **bounded, session-scoped queue of confirmed transcription segments** that could not be delivered reliably, with safe ordering and explicit outcomes (confirmed inserted / definitely not inserted / ambiguous). No silent drops, unbounded memory, or automatic replay after ambiguous insertion.
12. Offer a minimal **contextual recovery** path (retry after explicitly reselecting a supported field when safe; copy uninserted text as a fallback). Avoid page-wide warnings, extra permanent controls or unsolicited clipboard writes; do not overwrite the user's clipboard without an explicit user action.
13. When the editor becomes writable again, only retry segments known **not** to have been inserted, and only to the same verified/re-authorized target. Unknown/ambiguous outcomes require user review to avoid duplicate text. Keep the user informed with concise in-context error state rather than a silent stop.
14. Maintain Stop/Cancel semantics, local-only processing, permission revocation safety, pagehide/navigation cleanup, cross-tab/document ownership, capability validation, backpressure, audio watchdogs, and resource cleanup. **Real** microphone disconnects, overloaded audio pipelines, or lost security authorization should still stop the appropriate session.
15. For `FocusedInputTextOutputNode`, preserve its existing graph/session failure isolation and authorization; a failed delivery should be reported for that output without causing unrelated graph branches to stop.

### D. Test like real framework editors

16. Add automated browser fixture pages using representative **controlled React inputs, ProseMirror, Lexical, Draft.js and Quill-style editors**, with stateful re-rendering (not only a bare `contenteditable` div). Prefer real editor dependencies or sufficiently faithful minimal fixtures over mocks that cannot catch reconciliation bugs.
17. Cover: app-state update, multi-segment dictation, text inserted at caret / replacing selection, multiline, composition/IME, Undo/Redo, manual edits between segments, focus change, DOM replacement/rerender, ambiguous insertion, duplicate-avoidance, safe recovery, and accessibility.
18. Include smoke scenarios modeled on X post, ChatGPT and Claude composers; site-specific production adaptations only if a reproducible failing case remains. Do not require logged-in live sites or manual human approval as a blocking CI gate.
19. Add capture/relay regression coverage showing that an insertion rejection **does not** terminate an otherwise healthy mic/ASR session, but a genuine track end, permission revocation or audio transport failure still does.
20. Preserve the existing simpler `input`, `textarea`, and plain `contenteditable` behavior and all tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Eligible ProseMirror/Lexical/Draft.js/Quill-like editors can expose the website mic rather than being unconditionally excluded, subject to security/read-only checks.
- [ ] Transcribed **final** text appears in a supported editor and persists through its framework's next state render, with correct caret/selection, no duplicate/lost text and working Undo where available.
- [ ] Dictation is usable through representative X / ChatGPT / Claude-style editor fixtures without framework-specific hacks in the general path.
- [ ] Ordinary inputs/textareas and the existing page output Node do not regress.
- [ ] Temporary insertion failure or editor re-render does **not unnecessarily stop the microphone**; uninserted text is bounded and recoverable, and insertion never silently targets another field.
- [ ] An ambiguous edit cannot be replayed automatically; replay/copy is user-mediated as appropriate.
- [ ] Permission loss, real mic failure, navigation and security invalidation still terminate/release resources safely.
- [ ] Automated browser/unit regression tests pass, without any required manual sign-off.

## Scope and non-goals

- This issue targets **general rich-editable compatibility and resilience**, not hardcoded X/ChatGPT/Claude site adapters, scraping, arbitrary DOM/page-world scripting, extension permission expansion, or online transcription.
- **No change to AI models** or inferred text content.
- Keep existing lean UI principles: introduce error/recovery UI only when needed, not redundant persistent explanations.
- If particular websites remain incompatible after general improvements, document the **specific reproducible case** for a **separate focused follow-up Issue**.

## Research pointers

- MDN: `document.execCommand()` remains deprecated but some editing commands preserve Undo; use as a carefully tested compatibility tool, not as a universal guarantee.
- ProseMirror / Lexical: editor frameworks maintain their own document/state models; synthetic events and direct DOM edits alone often do not update the app.
- Open-source research candidates: OpenCues and LocalDictate; evaluate approaches critically without assuming their methods work on every editor.
